full_judgment:
3. Facts relevant for the disposal of this petition are that respondent Nos. 1-16 instituted Title Suit No. 34. of 1981 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Satkhira against the petitioner and 11 others for declaration of title to the suit land and confirmation of possession therein alleging, inter alia, that the plaintiffs acquired title to the suit land on the basis of settlement from the landlord Narendra Nath Laha by a registered patta dated 14th July, 1944 on payment of salami of Tk. 7,000/-, and at the rental of Tk.150/- in the benami of Khairul Alam and on the same day a kabuliyat was executed in favour of the landlord by the said Khairul Alam Khan. Since the date of settlement the plaintiffs have been in possession of the suit land. It is also alleged that the plaintiff No.1 obtained delivery of the registered patta from the concerned Sub-Registrar's Office. The suit land was put to auction sale by the Government and one Abdus Rashid and others purchased the suit land. The aforesaid benamder Khairul Alam Khan filed a suit for setting aside the auction sale which was decreed on compromise and the sale was set aside. The plaintiffs further alleged that during preparation of P.R.R. Khatian, at the initial stage the suit land was recorded in the name of the plaintiffs but in final record the suit land was recorded wrongly in the khas khatian and such wrong record has clouded the plaintiff's title. 

 4. The defendant No.6, Government of Bangladesh, contested the suit by filing written statement contending that the suit land belonged to Narendra Nath Laha and it was his khas land and while in posses the suit land was acquired by the Government and was made khas and the suit land was correctly recorded in the khas khatian of the Government within the knowledge of the plaintiffs. It is further alleged that the Government is in possession of the suit land by leasing out the same on yearly basis to different persons and that the plaintiffs never took settlement of the suit land from Narendra Nath Laha and never got any patta or issued Pakhila to the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs procured some collusive and fictious papers with the help of the outgoing Nayeb of Laha Estate. It was further alleged that the settlement of the suit land in the benami of Khairul Alam Khan is a concocted story and that the alleged patta was never acted upon. The plaintiffs have no title or possession in the suit land. 

 7. We have heard the learned Attorney General appearing for the petitioner and Mr. M.A. Mannan, the learned counsel appearing for the added respondents. We have perused the judgments of the Courts below and the order of the High Court Division summarily rejecting the revision petition. Mr. Attorney General has taken as to the plaint and submitted that the plaintiffs stated in paragraph 3 that they took settlement of the suit land in the benami of Khairul Alam on the ground that if they had taken settlement in their names their co-sharers might have claimed right in the said property. Mr. Attorney General submitted, this claim is apparently false, and none of the plaintiffs witnesses proved the benami transaction by adducing any reliable evidence. Learned Attorney General further argued that they also failed to explain why they did not file the original patta had the suit land been taken settlement by them, inasmuch as, the patta would have been in their possession and that they also failed to show that they paid any rent to the ex-landlord after taking patta or to the Government after acquisition of rent receiving interest by the Government. This fact, according to the learned Attorney General, sufficiently proved that the plea of benami transaction is a myth with a view to grab the suit land taking advantage of the situation that Khairul Alam being an Indian citizen, there is noise to claim the suit land. Learned Attorney General finally argued that the High Court Division as well as the Courts below failed to consider these aspects of the matter and upon superficial consideration of the materials on record decreed the suit. 

 "I. Because, the alleged patta dated 14th July, 1944 haying allegedly granted by Narendra Chandra Laha in favour of Khairul Alam Khan and the instant suit having been filed by six plaintiffs from different places and they having claimed that Khairul Alam Khan was their benamdar, without determining the said issue, the trial court has decreed the suit and the Court of appeal below as well as the High Court Division have affirmed the said judgment without considering the said aspect of benami transaction and thereby committed error in decreeing the suit.
